en: The *Karmavācanā* for the Bhikṣuṇīs in Four Parts, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇavarman of Kasmīra during the Song Dynasty. 1.

The Method for Establishing Boundaries (*Sīmā-bandhana*). First: The ritual procedures for establishing various boundaries are identical to those for the monks (*bhikṣu*) mentioned above; the only difference is that one addresses them as "Elder Sisters" (*bhaginī*).

2. The Dharma for Receiving Precepts. Section Two: The Text for the Bhikṣuṇī’s Request for the Karmavācanā to Maintain a Following. If a bhikṣuṇī wishes to ordain others, she should go before the community of bhikṣuṇīs, bare her right shoulder, remove her leather sandals, and prostrate at the feet of the Saṃgha. Then, placing her right knee on the ground and joining her palms, she requests the karmavācanā for maintaining a following.
She makes this formal announcement:
"Venerable Sisters of the Sangha, please listen!
I, the bhikṣuṇī [Name], now request from the Sangha the permission to ordain others and bestow upon them the full precepts."
"May the Saṃgha listen as I ordain a person and confer the full precepts (upasampadā).
Thus it is said three times.
The *karmavācanā* for granting permission to maintain disciples: "Sisters of the Saṃgha, listen! May the Saṃgha listen!"
This nun, [Name], now requests the Saṃgha for permission to ordain others and bestow upon them the full precepts (upasampadā).
If it is the proper time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, may the Saṃgha now permit the nun [Name] to ordain others and bestow upon them the full precepts.
The motion is thus stated.
Venerable Sisters of the Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣuṇī [Name], now requests from the Saṃgha permission to ordain others and bestow upon them full ordination.
The Saṃgha now consents that the bhikṣuṇī [Name] shall ordain persons and bestow upon them full ordination (*upasampadā*).
Those of you, venerable sisters, who consent that the Saṃgha permits the bhikṣuṇī [Name] to ordain persons and bestow upon them full ordination, remain silent; those who do not consent, speak.
The Saṃgha has already granted its consent; the nun so-and-so has completed the ordination of a person by bestowing upon them the full precepts.
Since the Saṃgha consents and remains silent, this matter is thus upheld.
The Text on Ordaining a Śrāmaṇerikā: If one wishes to have their hair shaved within the monastery, they should inform the entire Saṃgha.
If the assembly is not in harmony, they should go from room to room to inform everyone;
if the assembly is in harmony, they should perform the formal announcement (jñapti), and only then may the hair be shaved.
The formal motion (*jñapti*) should be made as follows:
"Venerable Sisters of the Sangha, please listen!
This person, so-and-so, wishes to seek a haircut from so-and-so."
If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent that [the hair] of so-and-so be shaved.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*).
Having made this motion, the hair shall be shaved.
If one wishes to receive ordination within the monastery, they should inform the entire Saṃgha.
If the assembly is not in harmony, they should go from room to room to speak and let everyone know;
if the assembly is in harmony, they should perform the formal announcement (jñapti), and only then grant the ordination.
The formal motion (*jñapti*) should be made as follows:
"Venerable Sisters of the Sangha, please listen!
This person, so-and-so, wishes to seek ordination from so-and-so."
If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent and listen: I announce that [so-and-so] shall go forth.
One should perform the going forth in this manner.

Having instructed the one going forth to don the *kāṣāya*, he should be taught to bare his right shoulder, remove his leather sandals, place his right knee on the ground, join his palms, and make the following formal declaration (*jñapti*):
"I, the seeker [name], take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, and take refuge in the Saṃgha."
I now follow the Buddha to leave the household life; my preceptress is [Name]. The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is my World-Honored One.
Thus it is said three times.
I, [Name], am now finished taking refuge in the Buddha, finished taking refuge in the Dharma, and finished taking refuge in the Saṅgha.
I have now followed the Buddha into homelessness; [Name], the Bhikṣuṇī, is my preceptor. The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, is my World-Honored One.
Having likewise recited this three times, you should be granted the precepts:
"For as long as life lasts, you must not kill living beings.
This is the śrāmaṇerikā precept; can you uphold it?"
She replies, "I can. "For as long as life lasts, you must not steal.
This is a śrāmaṇerikā precept; can you uphold it?"
She replies, "I can. "For as long as life lasts, one must not engage in sexual misconduct.
This is a precept of the śrāmaṇerī; can you uphold it?"
He replies, "I can. "For as long as life lasts, you must not speak falsely.
This is a precept for śrāmaṇerikās; can you uphold it?"
He replies, “I can. “For as long as life lasts, you must not drink alcohol.
This is a precept for a śrāmaṇerikā; can you uphold it?”
She replies, "I can.
"For as long as life lasts, you must not wear flower garlands nor smear your body with fragrant oils.
This is a śrāmaṇerikā precept; can you uphold it?"
She replies, "I can. "For as long as life lasts, you must not engage in singing, dancing, or theatrical performances, nor should you watch or listen to them.
This is the precept of a śrāmaṇerikā; can you uphold it?"
She replies, "I can.
"For as long as life lasts, you must not sit upon high, wide, or large beds.
This is a precept for śrāmaṇerikās; can you uphold it?"
She replies, “I can.
“For as long as life lasts, you must not grasp or hold gold, silver, or precious objects, whether raw or refined.
This is the precept for a śrāmaṇerikā; can you uphold it?”
She replies, "I can.
"For as long as life lasts, you must not eat at improper times.
This is a śrāmaṇerikā precept; can you uphold it?"
She replies, "I can.
Thus, regarding these ten precepts for a śrāmaṇerikā:
for as long as life lasts, you must not violate them; are you able to uphold them?
He replies, "I am able.
You have now completed receiving the precepts; you should make offerings to the Three Jewels:
the Buddha Jewel, the Dharma Jewel, and the Sangha Jewel.
One should cultivate the three types of practice:
sitting in meditation, reciting the sūtras, and assisting in communal affairs.

It is permitted for a girl who is eighteen years old to study the precepts for two years; when she reaches twenty years of age, she shall receive full ordination before the dual assembly of monks and nuns.
If she is ten years of age and has previously been married, she is permitted to train in the precepts for two years; once she has reached twelve years of age, she shall be granted full ordination.
She should be granted the two-year training in the precepts in this manner.

The Text on the Six Dharmas for the Śikṣamāṇā: A śrāmaṇerī should go before the community of bhikṣuṇīs, bare her right shoulder, remove her leather sandals, and, having prostrated at the feet of the bhikṣuṇī-saṃgha, place her right knee on the ground and join her palms, making this declaration:
"Venerable Sisters of the Saṃgha, please listen!"
I, the śrāmaṇerī [Name], now request from the Saṃgha the two-year training in the precepts, with the bhikṣuṇī [Name] as my upādhyāyī.
May the Saṃgha grant me deliverance out of compassion.
Thus it should be said three times.

Having led the śrāmaṇerī to a place where she can hear but not see [the assembly], one among the community who is capable of performing the *karmavācanā* should make the formal announcement (*jñapti*) as follows:
"Venerable sisters of the Saṃgha, listen!..."
This śrāmaṇerikā, [name], now requests from the Saṃgha the two-year training in the precepts, with the bhikṣuṇī [name] as her preceptor (upādhyāyikā).

If it is the proper time for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent and listen: the Saṃgha now grants this śrāmaṇerikā, [name], the two-year training in the precepts, with the bhikṣuṇī [name] as her preceptor.
The motion is as follows:
"Venerable Sisters of the Sangha, please listen!
This śrāmaṇerikā [Name], now requests from the Sangha two years of training in the precepts, with [Name] as her precept-mother (upādhyāyikā)."
The Sangha now grants two years of training in the precepts to the śrāmaṇerikā [Name], with [Name] as her precept-mother (upādhyāyikā).

Which of you, noble sisters, approves of the Sangha granting two years of training in the precepts to the śrāmaṇerikā [Name], with [Name] as her precept-mother? Those who approve remain silent; those who do not approve speak.
This is the first *karmavācanā*.
Thus it is said three times.
"The Saṃgha has already consented to grant the two-year training in the precepts to the śrāmaṇerikā [Name], with [Name] as her precept-mother; this is concluded."
The Saṃgha consents, as it remains silent; thus this matter is upheld.
It should be granted in this manner: "Noble one [Name], listen attentively!
The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, has proclaimed six rules which must not be transgressed."
One must not engage in sexual intercourse.
If a śikṣamāṇā engages in sexual intercourse,
she is no longer a śikṣamāṇā, nor is she a daughter of the Śākya clan.
If one touches the body of a man with a defiled mind, one violates the precepts and should receive the precepts again.
Within this, for as long as life lasts, you must not commit such an offense; can you maintain this?
She replies, "I can. She must not commit theft, even of so much as a blade of grass or a leaf.

If a śikṣamāṇā takes five kārṣāpaṇas or more than five kārṣāpaṇas—whether she takes it herself or instructs another to take it; whether she cuts it herself or instructs another to cut it; whether she breaks it herself or instructs another to break it; or whether she burns it, buries it, or alters its color; [she commits an offense].
She is no longer a *śikṣamāṇā*, nor is she a daughter of the Śākya clan.
If she takes property worth less than five *māṣakas*, her precepts are impaired and she must receive the ordination again.
Within this, for as long as life lasts, you must not commit such an offense; can you uphold this?
She replies, "I can. Yet she must not intentionally take the life of any living being, even so small as an ant.

If a śikṣamāṇā intentionally takes a human life with her own hand, or seeks out a knife to give to another, or instructs someone to die, encourages death, or praises death; or if she administers non-medicinal substances, causes an abortion, or performs suppressive incantations and spells—whether doing these herself or instructing another to do so; [she commits an offense.]
She is neither a śikṣamāṇā nor a daughter of the Śākya clan.
If she has taken the life of an animal that cannot undergo transformation, she is deficient in the precepts and should receive the ordination again.
Within this, for as long as life lasts, you must not commit any transgression;
can you uphold this? He replies, "I can.
You must not speak falsely, even in jest.

If a śikṣamāṇā, being untrue and not possessing [such qualities] herself, falsely claims to have attained the state of a superior person, saying she has attained dhyāna, liberation, samādhi, or right reception; or that she has attained the fruit of a srotāpanna, sakṛdāgāmin, anāgāmin, or arhat; or says that devas, nāgas, or spirits come to make offerings to her—she is no longer a śikṣamāṇā, nor is she a daughter of the Śākya clan.
If one intentionally utters a falsehood within the assembly, the precepts are impaired and one must receive them again.
Within this, for as long as life lasts, you must not commit an offense; can you uphold this?
She replies, "I can. She must not eat at improper times.
If a śikṣamāṇā eats at an improper time, she commits an offense and should be given the precepts again.
Within this, for as long as life lasts, you must not commit any transgression;
can you uphold this? He replied, "I can.
You must not drink alcohol.
If a śikṣamāṇā drinks alcohol, she commits a transgression of the precepts and must receive the precepts again.
Within this, for as long as life lasts, you must not commit this offense; can you maintain it?
She replied, "I can.
A śikṣamāṇā should train in all the precepts of the bhikṣuṇīs, except for eating after the proper time and eating food that she has received for herself.

The Procedure for a Śikṣamāṇā Receiving Full Ordination: If a śikṣamāṇā has completed her training in the precepts and is twenty years of age—or, in the case of a girl who has undergone the preliminary rite, twelve years of age—she should be granted full ordination.
First, go among the bhikṣuṇī-saṃgha and request a preceptor, speaking as follows:
"Sister, please attend to me with one-pointed mind!
I, [Name], seek you, Venerable Lady, to be my preceptor; I pray that you will act as my preceptor."
"Because of my reliance upon the Āryā, I have received the full ordination.
Thus it should be said three times.
The precept-giving nun (upādhyāyī) should respond, "So be it."

It should be upheld in this manner: the person receiving the precepts should move away from where they can hear [the assembly] and stand where they can see it, and a teacher of instruction should be appointed.
Among them, the precept master should ask as follows:
"Who in this assembly is able to act as the teacher of instruction for [so-and-so]?"
If there is such a person, they should reply, "I am able.
At that time, the Preceptor of the Precepts (Śīlācārya) should immediately make the formal announcement (*jñapti*):
"May the noble Sisters of the Saṃgha listen!..."
This [person], so-and-so, seeks to receive the full ordination from the preceptor nun, so-and-so.
If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent that so-and-so shall serve as the instructor.
The announcement is thus made.
The preceptor should go to the place where the candidate for ordination is and say:
"Are these the *antarvāsa*, the *uttarāsaṅga*, and the *saṃghāṭī*; this *saṃkakṣikā* and the shoulder-covering cloth; and these robes and bowl yours?"
He replied, "I have it.
"Good woman, listen attentively!
Now is the time for truth. I shall now question you; if you have it, say you have it; if you do not, you should say you do not."
Have you not committed an offense involving a border-line transgression?
Have you not committed an offense against a bhikṣu of pure conduct?
Have you not received the precepts with a thieving mind?
Have you not broken [the precepts]? Are you not an adherent of internal or external paths? Are you not a eunuch?
Have you not killed your father?
Have you not killed your mother?
Have you not killed a true person, an Arhat?
Have you not caused a schism in the Saṃgha?
Did you not, with an evil mind, draw blood from the body of a Buddha?
Are you not a non-human being? Are you not an animal?
Are you not of both genders?
What is your name? And what is the name of your preceptress?
"Have you reached the required age?
Are your robes and alms bowl complete?
Have your parents and husband given their permission?"
Are you not in debt? Are you not a slave? Are you a woman?
Women have such diseases as leprosy,
white leprosy, consumption, insanity, dual sexual organs, conjoined vaginal and urinary tracts, narrow vaginas, constant leakage of urine and feces, and constant discharge of mucus and saliva.
"Do you have any such illnesses?
If he answers "No," one should say to him:
"As I have just asked you, so shall the Sangha also ask you."
Just as you have answered me previously, you should answer likewise within the Saṃgha.

Once the instructor has finished questioning you, you should go into the midst of the Saṃgha and stand at a place where you can reach [the instructor] with an outstretched hand, maintaining your usual dignified demeanor.
The formal announcement (*jñapti*) should be made as follows: "Sisters of the Saṃgha, please listen!
This [person], so-and-so, seeks to receive the full ordination (*upasampadā*) from the preceptor nun (upādhyāyinī), so-and-so."
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, I have finished instructing [the candidate]; please allow her to come.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*). He should then say to her, "Come."

Once she has arrived, you should give her the robes and bowl, instruct her to prostrate at the feet of the Sangha, and have her kneel with palms joined before the Preceptor (Śikṣamāṇācāryā) and make this request:
"Sister Sangha, please listen!"
I, [Name], seek to receive the full ordination from the preceptor nun [Name].
I, [Name], now request the Saṃgha to grant me the full ordination, with [Name] as my preceptor nun.
"May the Saṃgha deliver me, out of compassion.
Thus he should say three times.
Therein, the preceptor should make the formal motion (jñapti):
Venerable Sisters of the Sangha, listen!
This [person], so-and-so, seeks to receive the full ordination from the preceptor nun so-and-so.
This so-and-so now requests the Sangha for the bestowal of the full ordination, with the preceptor nun so-and-so.
"If it is the time for the Sangha and the Sangha is willing to listen, I shall ask about matters concerning obstacles.
This is the formal announcement (*jñapti*). Listen attentively!"
This is now a time of truth; I now question you: if there is, you should say there is; if there is not, you should say there is not.
Have you not committed a pārājika offense?
Have you not violated a bhikṣu of pure conduct?
"Have you not received the precepts with a thieving mind?
Have you not broken the precepts of either the inner or outer paths? Are you not a eunuch?"
Have you not killed your father?
Have you not killed your mother?
Have you not killed a true person, an Arhat?
Have you not caused a schism in the Saṃgha?
Have you not, with an evil mind, shed the blood of a Buddha?
Are you not a non-human being?
Are you not an animal?
Are you not a hermaphrodite? What is your name?
What is the name of your preceptress?
Have you reached the required age?
Are your robes and alms bowl complete?
"Do your parents and husband permit you?
Are you not in debt? Are you not a slave?"
"Are you a woman? Women have such various ailments as leprosy,
white leprosy, consumption, insanity, hermaphroditism, the fusion of the two orifices, a narrow orifice, and the constant leakage of urine and excrement."
"Do you have any such illnesses?
If he answers, "No," one should perform the formal announcement (*jñapti*) as follows:
Venerable Sisters of the Sangha, listen!
This [name], from the preceptress [name], seeks to receive the full ordination.
This [name] now requests the Sangha for the full ordination, with [name] as her preceptress.
So-and-so declares himself pure, free from obstacles, twenty years of age, and fully equipped with robes and bowl.
If the time has come for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent; the Saṃgha now confers the full ordination upon So-and-so, with So-and-so as the preceptress-ni (upādhyāyikā).
The motion is thus stated.
Venerable Sisters of the Saṃgha, listen!
This [person], so-and-so, seeks to receive the full ordination from the preceptor nun, so-and-so.
This [person], so-and-so, now requests from the Saṃgha the full ordination, with the preceptor nun so-and-so.
So-and-so has personally declared herself pure, free from all obstacles, of full age, and possessed of the robes and bowl.
The Sangha now confers the full ordination upon [Name], with [Name] as the preceptress-ni.

Which of you venerable sisters approves of the Sangha now conferring the full ordination upon [Name] with [Name] as the preceptress-ni? Those who approve remain silent; those who do not approve speak.
This is the first *karmavācanā*.
The second and third are also spoken in this manner.
The Sangha has already consented; the full ordination for [Name] has been completed, with [Name] as the preceptress (*upādhyāyinī*).
The Saṃgha having consented by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.

Regarding the procedure for a nun to go before the Bhikṣu-saṃgha to receive the full ordination (*upasampadā*): the candidate for ordination, together with the Bhikṣuṇī-saṃgha, goes to the Bhikṣu-saṃgha; having prostrated at the feet of the Saṃgha, she places her right knee on the ground, joins her palms, and speaks as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, please listen!"
I, [Name], seek to receive the full ordination from the preceptor nun [Name].
I, [Name], now request the Sangha to grant me the full ordination, with [Name] as my preceptor nun.
"May the Sangha rescue me out of compassion.
Thus he should say three times.
At this point, the preceptor should inquire about various obstacles and make the formal announcement (*jñapti*):
Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This [person], so-and-so, seeks to receive the full ordination from the preceptor nun, so-and-so.
This [person], so-and-so, now requests the Saṃgha for the full ordination, with the preceptor nun, so-and-so, acting as her preceptor.
If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha listen with patience as I inquire about matters concerning obstacles.
This is the formal announcement (*jñapti*).
Listen attentively, virtuous woman!
Now is the time for truth, the time for speaking the reality. I now ask you: if there is, you should say there is; if there is not, you should say there is not.
Have you not committed a bordering offense?
Have you not committed an offense against a bhikṣu of pure conduct?
Have you not received the precepts with a thieving mind?
Have you not broken [the vows of] either the inner or outer paths?
Are you not a eunuch?
Have you not killed your father?
Have you not killed your mother?
Have you not killed a true person, an Arhat?
Have you not caused a schism in the Saṃgha?
Have you not, with an evil mind, shed the blood of a Buddha?
Are you not a non-human? Are you not an animal?
Are you not a hermaphrodite?
"What is your name? What is the name of your preceptor nun?
Have you reached twenty years of age?"
Are your robes and alms bowl complete?
Have your parents and husband given you their permission?
Are you free from debt?
Are you not a slave?
Are you a woman? Women have such various ailments as these:

Leprosy, white leprosy, consumption, insanity, being of two sexual organs, having two conjoined orifices, having a narrow orifice, constant leakage of urine and feces, and constant discharge of mucus and saliva.
"Do you have any such illnesses? If he answers "No," one should ask:
"Have you studied the precepts?"
"Is it pure? She should reply, "My training in the precepts is pure.
Then she should ask the other bhikṣuṇīs:
"Has such-and-such person studied the precepts? Is he pure?
He replies, "I have studied the precepts and am pure."
Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This [person], so-and-so, seeks to receive the full ordination from the preceptor nun so-and-so.
This so-and-so now requests the Saṃgha to grant her the full ordination, with so-and-so as her preceptor nun.
So-and-so has declared herself pure, free from obstacles, of full age, possessed of robes and bowl, and having trained in the purity of the precepts.
If it is the time for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent; the Saṃgha now confers the Upasampadā upon So-and-so, with the Bhikṣuṇī So-and-so as her Preceptor.
The motion is thus:
"Venerable Saṃgha, please listen!
This person, so-and-so, seeks to receive the full ordination from the preceptor nun, so-and-so."
This person, [Name], now requests from the Saṃgha the reception of the full ordination, with the Bhikṣuṇī [Name] as preceptor.
This person has declared herself to be pure, free from all obstacles, of age, fully possessed of robes and bowl, and having already trained in the purity of the precepts.
The Sangha now confers the full ordination upon [Name], with [Name] as the preceptor-ni.
Those elders who consent to the Sangha conferring the full ordination upon [Name] with [Name] as the preceptor-ni should remain silent; those who do not consent should speak.
This is the first *karmavācanā*.
Thus it is said three times.
The Saṃgha has already granted its consent; the full ordination for [Name] has been completed, with [Name] as the *upādhyāyī* nun.
The Saṃgha consents, as it remains silent; thus this matter is upheld.
Listen attentively, virtuous woman!
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has proclaimed the eight pārājika rules. If a bhikṣuṇī violates them, she is no longer a bhikṣuṇī, nor is she a daughter of the Śākya clan.
One must not commit impure conduct or engage in sexual intercourse.
If a bhikṣuṇī commits impure conduct or engages in sexual intercourse, even with an animal;
she is no longer a bhikṣuṇī, nor is she a daughter of the Śākya clan.
Within this, you must not commit any transgression for as long as life lasts;
can you maintain this? Answer: "I can.
You must not steal, even so much as a blade of grass or a leaf.

If a bhikṣuṇī steals five coins or more than five coins from another person—whether she takes them herself or instructs another to take them, whether she cuts them herself or instructs another to cut them, whether she breaks them herself or instructs another to break them, or whether she burns them, buries them, or alters their color—she is no longer a bhikṣuṇī;
she is no longer a daughter of the Śākya clan.
Within this, for as long as life lasts, you must not commit any transgression;
can you uphold this? He replied, "I can.
You must not take the life of any sentient being, even down to an ant.

If a bhikṣuṇī herself takes the life of a human being with her own hand, hands a weapon to another, instructs someone to die, praises death, encourages death, gives another a non-medicinal substance, causes an abortion, performs malevolent incantations or sorcery, or employs such means herself or instructs another to employ such means;
she is no longer a bhikṣuṇī, nor a daughter of the Śākya clan.
Within this, for as long as life lasts, you must not commit any transgression;
can you uphold this? Answer: "I can.
You must not speak falsely, even in jest.

If a bhikṣuṇī, being untrue and possessing nothing herself, falsely claims to have attained the state of a superior person—asserting that she has attained dhyāna, liberation, samādhi, or right reception; or that she has attained the fruit of srotāpanna, sakṛdāgāmin, anāgāmin, or arhat; or saying that devas, nāgas, or yakṣas come to make offerings to her—she is not a bhikṣuṇī, nor is she a daughter of the Śākya clan.
Within this, for as long as life lasts, you must not commit any transgression;
can you maintain this? He replies, "I can.
One must not engage in physical contact, even with an animal.

That bhikṣuṇī admonished the other bhikṣuṇī, saying: "Sister!..."

Regarding the inner protection and rectification of the Saṃgha, the formal acts of censure and punishment (saṃgha-karman) are elucidated in the Vinaya Piṭaka. The essential core of the Saṃgha’s True Dharma consists of three points; therefore, the Council declared:
"This is the Dharma, this is the Vinaya, this is the teaching of the Buddha."
“Dharma” refers to the five kinds of practices of renunciation.

What are these five? First, transcendence rather than worldly dharmas; second, crossing over rather than the dharma of grasping; third, desirelessness rather than having desires; fourth, freedom from fetters rather than having fetters; fifth, not drawing near to birth and death rather than drawing near to them.
Vinaya refers to the five kinds of practices leading to liberation.

What are the five? First, having few desires rather than many; second, being content rather than insatiable; third, being easy to guard rather than difficult to guard; fourth, being easy to support rather than difficult to support; and fifth, possessing wisdom rather than ignorance.
That which is taught by the Buddha refers to five kinds of disciplinary instructions.

What are the five? First, the prohibition of what constitutes an offense; second, the permission of what is not an offense; third, when there is a deficiency in either the prohibitions or the permissions, to address it according to the Dharma; fourth, to repeatedly subdue those who violate the rules through admonition; and fifth, to affectionately cherish and praise genuine virtues.
Therefore, the Sūtra says:
"The True Dharma abides; the True Dharma perishes.
This is what it means.
Regarding those who transmit this Dharma, there are likewise three types; thus the holy teachings state:
"One who knows the Dharma, one who knows the Vinaya, and one who knows the Mātṛkā.
One who knows the Dharma refers to one who skillfully upholds the Sūtra Piṭaka, such as:
"Ānanda and others who know the Vinaya" refers to those who skillfully uphold the Piṭaka of Vinaya,
such as Upāli and others.
Those who know the *Māyī* (Vinaya) are those skilled in instruction and entrusted with the profound governing principles,
such as Mahākāśyapa and others. Therefore,

if anyone wishes to illuminate the traces of the sages, to cause the Way and its teachings to flourish, and to continue their legacy for future generations without interruption, who could it be other than these?
There are five methods for entering an assembly. What are the five?
First, one should do so with a mind of loving-kindness;
2. One should humble oneself like a cloth used for wiping dust;
3. One should be well-versed in the dignified deportment of sitting, rising, ascending, and descending;
4. One should not speak of mundane matters in a distracted manner, but should preach the Dharma for the assembly or request others to do so.
5. If one sees something improper within the Saṃgha and the mind cannot endure it with equanimity, one should maintain silence.
There are five kinds of lawful silence. What are the five?

1. Remaining silent when seeing others act contrary to the Dharma; 2. Remaining silent when not obtaining companions; 3. Remaining silent when committing a grave offense; 4. Remaining silent while living together; 5. Remaining silent within the boundaries of the communal residence.
There are five kinds of improper silence. What are the five?
First, when a formal act (*karmavācanā*) is performed in accordance with the Dharma, one remains silent and acquiesces despite having a different mind.
2. To remain silent when obtaining a companion who shares one’s same view;
3. To remain silent upon seeing a minor offense;
4. To remain silent while performing the *parivāsa* (probation) for another.
5. Remaining silent on the boundary of the precept-platform (*sīmā*).
There are five kinds of acts involving forfeiture (*naiḥsargika-pāyattika*). What are the five?
1. A bhikṣu commits an offense. Another bhikṣu asks him:
"Do you see that you have committed an offense? He replies:
"I do not see it. He said: "If you see your transgression, you should confess it."
2. When a bhikṣu has committed an offense, another bhikṣu asks him:
“Do you see that you have committed an offense? He replies:
"I do not see it.
He said: "If you see your transgression, you should confess it before the Saṃgha."
3. A bhikṣu commits an offense, and another bhikṣu asks him:
"Do you see that you have committed an offense? He replies:
"I do not see it.
He said, "If you see your transgression, you should confess it before this Sangha."
4. When a bhikṣu has committed an offense, another bhikṣu asks him:
"Do you see that you have committed an offense? He replies:
"If you do not see [your fault]," the community of monks should reject his speech, saying:

"Since you do not see your offense, wherever you go, we shall not allow you to participate in the *poṣadha*. Just as a wild horse that is difficult to tame is discarded along with its halter and tethering stake, so too are you."
5. When a bhikṣu has committed an offense, another bhikṣu asks him:
"Do you see that you have committed an offense? He replies:
“I did not see it.
He should then undergo the formal act of suspension for denial (*adarśana-utkṣepa-karman*) within the Saṃgha.

we shall act as your companions.
Thus they cause disputes to arise where none existed before, and they fail to resolve disputes that already exist.

If the time is ripe for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha, out of compassion, grant its consent to perform a *tarjanīya-karman* (act of censure) against the bhikṣu so-and-so; should he again engage in quarreling or mutual verbal abuse hereafter, the Saṃgha shall further increase his punishment.
The announcement is as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣu, so-and-so, delights in quarreling and mutual abuse; his mouth spews swords and blades, and he seeks out the faults of others."
Having already engaged in mutual strife themselves, if there are other bhikṣus who are also quarreling, they go to them and urge them, saying:
"Exert yourselves! Do not be inferior to others!"
"You possess great wisdom and extensive learning, your wealth is superior, and you have many friends;
we shall act as your companions.
Thus they cause disputes to arise where none existed before, and they fail to resolve disputes that already exist.
The Sangha is performing a *tarjanīya-karman* (act of censure) against the bhikṣu [Name].

Which elders approve of the Sangha’s performance of the *tarjanīya-karman* against the bhikṣu [Name], such that if he should again engage in quarreling or mutual abuse, the community of monks shall further increase his punishment? Those who approve should remain silent; those who do not approve should speak.
This is the first *karmavācanā*.
Thus it is said three times.
The Saṃgha has consented; the act of censure (*tarjanīyakarman*) has been completed for the monk so-and-so.
Since the Saṃgha remains silent, this matter is thus upheld.
Having performed the *karmavācanā*, thirty-five matters are to be revoked from him to bring about his subjugation.
Later, if he becomes compliant and repents, the Saṃgha should restore the revocation of the *karmavācanā*.

The Text for the Karmavācanā of Assigning the Place of Offense: First, one performs the formal accusation (*udghātana*), the reminder (*smṛti*), and the assignment of the offense; thereafter, one performs the *karmavācanā*.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!..."
This bhikṣu, so-and-so, is devoid of shame and lacks remorse; he has committed many transgressions, which have been seen, heard, or suspected.
He first claimed that he had committed them, yet later claimed that he had not; his earlier and later statements are contradictory.
If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha listen with patience: the Saṃgha now grants the *karmavācanā* for the place of offense to the bhikṣu [Name].
This is the motion (*jñapti*).
Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣu, so-and-so, is devoid of shame and lacks remorse; he has committed many offenses regarding which there is what has been seen, heard, and suspected.
He previously claimed he had committed them, yet later claimed he had not; his earlier and later statements are contradictory.
The Saṃgha now grants this bhikṣu, so-and-so, the *karmavācanā* for the place of offense.

"Whichever elders approve of the Saṃgha now performing the *karmavācanā* for the formal act of assigning a place of penance to the bhikṣu so-and-so, let them remain silent; whoever does not approve, let them speak.
This is the first *karmavācanā*."
Thus it was said three times.
The Sangha has already consented; the *karmavācanā* for the formal act of assigning the offense to the monk so-and-so is completed.
Because the Sangha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.
Once the *karmavācanā* has been performed, one should cause him to undergo subjugation by means of thirty-five matters.
Later, if he complies and reforms, the Saṃgha should restore him by revoking the *karmavācanā*.

The Text for the Formal Act of Banishment by Exclusion: First, one performs the act of formal accusation, the act of calling to mind, and the assignment of the offense; thereafter, the formal act is performed.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣu, so-and-so, has committed such-and-such a pārājika offense."

If it is the proper time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, let the Saṃgha now perform the formal act of *parivāsa* (banishment) against the monk so-and-so for a *pārājika* offense: he shall not dwell together with the community, nor shall he engage in communal affairs.
The motion is thus stated.
Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣu, so-and-so, has committed such-and-such a pārājika offense.
The Saṃgha now performs the formal act of *pārājika* expulsion for the monk so-and-so, such that he shall not dwell together with the community and shall not engage in communal affairs.

Those elders who consent to the Saṃgha’s performance of the *pārājika* expulsion for the monk so-and-so, such that he shall not dwell together with the community and shall not engage in communal affairs, remain silent; those who do not consent, speak.
This is the first *karmavācanā*.
Thus it is said three times.

The Saṃgha has already consented to the formal act of suspension for the pārājika offense against the monk so-and-so; he shall not dwell together [with the Saṃgha] and shall not participate in communal affairs. The matter is concluded.
Since the Saṃgha remains silent, this matter is thus upheld. This is a permanent expulsion (*nigarhaṇīya-karman*), for which there is no method of rehabilitation.
These latter three *karman* procedures are all disciplinary measures; they are categorized into three grades solely based on the gravity of the transgressions.

The *karma* of prior reprimand (*prātimokṣa*) and so forth are methods of discipline (*vinaya*); the *karma* of the locus of offense (*āpattisthāna*) and so forth are methods of subjugation (*nigraha*); and the *karma* of banishment for extinction (*pravāsanīya*) and so forth are methods of expulsion (*niḥsaraṇa*).
Therefore, the Sūtra says: "Those who should be disciplined, one disciplines; those who should be subjugated, one subjugates; those who should be punished and excluded, one punishes and excludes."

If one were to speak according to specific matters, the *karmas* (formal acts) would not be limited to one; they are fully elucidated in the Vinaya scriptures, so how could they possibly be collected here in their entirety?
Therefore, each shall be treated according to its own category, with only a single *karman* being cited as a standard model, while the remaining types may be understood by analogy thereto.

The *Biqiuni Jie-mo Fa* (Method of Bhikṣuṇī Karmavācanā) in one fascicle: Examining this single fascicle of the *Karmavācanā*, the Song edition and the Guo edition are identical, whereas the Dan edition differs from both of them.

Why is this? Upon examining the present edition from Dan, its textual meaning largely accords with that collected by Huaisu; furthermore, its beginning and end follow a coherent sequence that is worth observing. Knowing it to be the authentic original translation by Guṇavarman, we have therefore included it in the canon.
The versions of that country and the two Song editions are extremely disordered.

Regarding the general sequence for a nun’s ordination from beginning to end: first she seeks to leave the household life; second, she receives the ten precepts and trains in the Dharma; after two years, she receives full ordination (*upasampadā*); only after a long period does she then request the *karmavācanā* for maintaining a retinue to ordain others and bestow the precepts—this is the proper order.
In this second version, the text for requesting an upādhyāya regarding the six dharmas is reused as the text for a śrāmaṇera requesting the ten precepts; this is the first confusion.
Furthermore, the text for requesting permission to maintain a following is appended before the reception of the full precepts; this is the second confusion.
Whenever a *bhikṣuṇī* receives the precepts, she first receives them from within the community of *bhikṣuṇīs*, and subsequently proceeds to the community of *bhikṣus* to receive them;
the second text states:
"The two assemblies of monks grant their consent."
To not distinguish between the preceding and succeeding [rules] constitutes the third disorder.

Within the six rules for training in the precepts, the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya* (Sifen lü) places eating at improper times and drinking alcohol as the fifth and sixth, whereas the other two versions place the eight matters of physical contact as the fifth and sixth; this is the fourth disorder.
Since the title itself states "Nikāya-kamma" (The Karmavācanā for Bhikṣuṇīs),

yet both versions contain the methods for bhikṣus ordaining śrāmaṇeras, the methods for śrāmaṇeras receiving the ten precepts, and the methods for bhikṣus receiving full ordination; this is the fifth disorder.
The *Kaiyuan lu* states: "Translated by Guṇavarman of the Song dynasty.
Both versions merely state:
"The Dharma for Women’s Ordination."
This is the sixth point of confusion.

Therefore, one should know that these two "originals" are merely the arbitrary conjectures and disordered excerpts of unverified people from later generations; they must not be relied upon or used, and for this reason, I have now separated them.
Have the bhikṣuṇīs who have not arrived declared their *chanda* (consent) and *viśuddhi* (purity)?
With the exception of the *sīmā* (boundary), there is no rule for receiving *chanda*.
At the time of the *pravāraṇā*, one should say:
Having announced the desire and the invitation,
one should further address the Saṃgha, saying:
"Sisters of the Saṃgha, please listen!"
"What is the Saṃgha currently doing?
One person among the Saṃgha should answer according to the preceding matter:
"The *karmavācanā* for so-and-so."

Regarding the method of establishing boundaries, two boundaries must not touch one another; an interval should be left between them. Furthermore, one must not establish a boundary across a rapidly flowing stream, except where there is a permanent bridge.

If one wishes to establish a *śīma-kuṭi* (ordination platform) within the great boundary (*mahā-sīmā*), first erect the four boundary markers for the *śīma-kuṭi*. Then, at a distance of one cubit outside these, erect the boundary markers for the interior of the great boundary; further outward, according to the desired distance, also erect the four boundary markers.
An elder resident bhikṣuṇī shall announce the boundaries and directions; from among the assembly, one capable of performing the *karmavācanā* shall be appointed to establish them.
One should first establish the great boundary (*mahāsīmā*) and subsequently establish the *śīmaṇḍala* (the precinct for the *poṣadha*).
If one wishes to proclaim the characteristics of this great boundary (mahā-sīmā), one first proceeds clockwise around the four directions starting from the southeastern corner of the outer boundary;
then one also proclaims the inner boundary, likewise completing a full circuit.
He says:
"That is the external boundary marker; this is the internal boundary marker; this completes one circuit of the internal and external markers of the great boundary.
Thus he proclaims three times.
If there is no inner *śīmaṇḍala* (戒場), one directly announces the outer boundary (*bāhya-lakṣaṇa*).
Regarding the ritual for establishing the great and small boundaries (*sīmā-bandhana*), the Saṃgha must assemble in its entirety; the acceptance of proxy votes (*chanda*) is not permitted.
The *karmavācanā* text for establishing the great boundary: "Sisters of the Saṃgha, listen!..."
The bhikṣuṇī so-and-so of this dwelling has proclaimed the marks of the great boundary (mahā-sīmā) in the four directions.

If the Saṃgha is ready and the Saṃgha permits, let the Saṃgha now, within these marks of the four directions, establish a great boundary as a single dwelling place for the purpose of a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa.
The motion is as follows:
"Venerable Sisters of the Sangha, please listen!
This Bhikṣuṇī [Name], residing at this location, proclaims the boundaries of the great perimeter (mahā-sīmā) in the four directions."
The Saṃgha now establishes a great boundary (*mahā-sīmā*) within these four directional markers, constituting a single residence and a single recitation of the precepts.

Those of you, sisters, who consent to the Saṃgha’s establishment of a great boundary within these four directional markers as a single residence and a single recitation of the precepts, remain silent; those who do not consent, speak.
The Saṃgha has already consented to establish a great boundary within these four marks, constituting a single residence and a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa.
Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter shall be maintained as such.

The *karmavācanā* for the delimitation of the boundary (*sīmābandha*) states: Originally, the establishment of the *śīmaṇḍala* (the site of the precepts) arose because it was difficult to assemble a large community at a single residence; therefore, this separate boundary was delimited to allow for the performance of necessary matters among the assembly at any time, and thus it cannot be immediately dissolved.

If one does not rely on a fixed dwelling place but performs the ritual merely for a temporary period, it shall be dissolved immediately upon the completion of the matter; it is not permissible not to dissolve it.
Sisters of the Sangha, listen!
The bhikṣuṇī [Name], residing at this location, has declared the marks of the small boundary on all four sides.

If it is the proper time for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent; the Saṃgha now establishes a *śīma-kaṇḍaka* (precept-platform) within these declared marks of the small boundary on all four sides.
The motion is as follows:
"Venerable Sisters of the Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣuṇī, so-and-so, residing in this location, has proclaimed the marks of the small boundary in the four directions."
The Saṃgha now intends to establish a *sīmā-kaṭhina* (precept platform) within these marks of the small boundary in the four directions.
Those of you, venerable sisters, who consent to the Saṃgha’s establishment of a *sīmā-kaṭhina* within these marks of the four directions, remain silent; those who do not consent, speak.
The Saṃgha has already consented; within these four boundaries, the establishment of the *sīmā-śīmaṇḍala* (precept enclosure) is completed.
Because the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter shall be upheld as such.
When the formal ritual (*karmavācanā*) for dissolving the great boundary (*mahāsīmā*) is being performed, some bhikṣuṇīs wish to make the boundary extensive, while others wish to make it narrow.
The Buddha said:
"From this day forward, if you wish to alter [the boundaries], first dissolve the previous boundary; thereafter, whether they are expanded or narrowed shall be according to your intention.
This dissolution must be performed through a *jñapti-dvitīya-karman* (a formal act consisting of one motion and one announcement).
Venerable Sisters of the Saṃgha, listen!
Now, the bhikṣuṇīs residing at this dwelling place share the same residence and the same recitation of the Prātimokṣa.
If the time is right for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, let the boundary be dissolved.
The motion is thus stated.
Venerable Sisters of the Sangha, listen!
The bhikṣuṇīs residing at this dwelling place, who share the same residence and the same recitation of the Prātimokṣa, now dissolve the boundary.

"Whichever sisters among you consent to the Sangha's lifting of the boundary for those dwelling in the same residence and reciting the Prātimokṣa together, remain silent; whoever does not consent, speak.
The Sangha has consented to lift the boundary for those dwelling in the same residence and reciting the Prātimokṣa together; this is concluded."
The Saṃgha consents by remaining silent; thus this matter is upheld as such.

Regarding the *karmavācanā* for establishing the *acīvarāsaṃsarga-sīmā* (the boundary where one is not separated from one’s robes): this boundary is established based on the characteristics of the *mahāsīmā* (great boundary) itself and possesses no distinct characteristics of its own; therefore, the wording of the text still refers to "this residence."
Venerable Sisters of the Sangha, listen!
This is a single dwelling place with a single recitation of the *Prātimokṣa*.

If the time has come for the Sangha and the Sangha permits, let the Sangha now establish the boundary for not losing one's robes (*akathina-sīmā*), excluding villages and the areas outside of villages.
The motion is as follows:
"Venerable Sisters of the Sangha, please listen!

This is a single residence with a single recitation of the precepts. The Sangha now establishes a 'no-loss-of-clothing' boundary (*akālacīvara-sīmā*), excluding villages and the areas outside of villages."

"Venerable sisters, those of you who consent to the Saṃgha’s formal establishment of a 'boundary for not losing one's robe' within this residence—sharing the same dwelling and the same recitation of the Prātimokṣa, excluding villages and the areas outside of villages—should remain silent; those who do not consent should speak."

The Saṃgha has already consented to establish, within this same dwelling place and for the same recitation of the Prātimokṣa, a boundary for the non-loss of robes, excluding villages and the areas outside of villages.
Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter shall be upheld accordingly.

The Ritual Text for Dissolving the *Amuktaka-cīvara* (Non-losing-of-robes) Boundary. Since the Great Boundary (*mahā-sīmā*) and the Non-losing-of-robes Boundary are both re-established within the same location, the sequence of dissolving and binding them is mutually inverted and differs [from the initial establishment].
If one wishes to dissolve [the boundaries], one should first dissolve the *acīvarāpatti-sīmā* (the boundary for not losing one's robe), and then dissolve the *mahāsīmā* (the great boundary).
Sisters of the Sangha, listen!
At this residence, the bhikṣuṇīs dwell together and perform the *poṣadha* (recitation of the precepts) together.
If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the Saṃgha now dissolve the *akalacīvara-sīmā*.
This is the motion (*jñapti*).
Sisters of the Saṃgha, listen!
The bhikṣuṇīs residing here, dwelling in the same location and reciting the precepts together, now dissolve the *acīvaram-avippavāsa-sīmā* (the boundary for not being separated from one's robes).

Those of you, sisters, who consent to the Sangha dissolving the *acīvaram-avippavāsa-sīmā* while dwelling in the same location and reciting the precepts together, remain silent; those who do not consent, speak.
The Sangha has already consented to this: the boundary for not losing one's robes is hereby dissolved for those dwelling in the same residence and reciting the Prātimokṣa together.
Since the Sangha consents by remaining silent, this matter shall be thus upheld.

The Karmavācanā for Establishing a Small Boundary (Sīmā): If, on the day of the Poṣadha, while bhikṣuṇīs are traveling along a road in a wilderness area without a village, they wish to recite the Prātimokṣa but find it difficult to assemble in great numbers and cannot achieve harmony, they are permitted to gather separately at one location away from the main path with their respective teachers, virtuous friends, and spiritual mentors, and establish a small boundary there to recite the Prātimokṣa.
Venerable Sisters of the Saṃgha, listen!
There are now this many bhikṣuṇīs assembled here.
If the time is right for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, let us establish a small boundary (sīmā).
The announcement is as follows:
"Venerable Sisters of the Sangha, please listen!
Now there are this many bhikṣuṇīs gathered to establish a small boundary (sīmā)."
"Venerable sisters, those who consent to the assembly of so many bhikṣuṇīs to formally establish a small boundary (sīmā) remain silent; those who do not consent speak.
The Saṃgha has finished consenting to the assembly of so many bhikṣuṇīs to formally establish the small boundary."
The Saṃgha remains silent; therefore, this matter is upheld as such.
[This is] the *karmavācanā* for dissolving a minor boundary (*khuddakasīmā*). Sisters of the Saṃgha, listen!
Now there are so many bhikṣuṇīs assembled here.
If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the small boundary (*kṣudra-sīmā*) at this location be dissolved.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*).
Venerable Sisters of the Saṃgha, listen!
Now, so many bhikṣuṇīs have assembled to dissolve this small boundary (sīmā) here.
Whoever among you, sisters, approves of the Sangha dissolving this small boundary here, remain silent; whoever does not approve, speak.
The Sangha has already consented to the resolution of this small boundary.
Because the Sangha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.

Regarding the *karmavācanā* for establishing a common *poṣadha* and a common distribution of offerings (*lābha*): If two residences are currently separate from one another and one now wishes to merge them so that they share a common *poṣadha* and a common distribution of offerings, one must first dissolve their respective original boundaries. Thereafter, boundary markers shall be erected throughout both residences to combine them into a single boundary.
The entire Saṃgha assembles in one place for the formal act (karmavācanā) of establishing the boundary.
"Venerable Sisters of the Saṃgha, listen!
As has been described regarding the characteristics of the boundary..."

If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha listen with patience: the Saṃgha now, at this place and that place, establishes a common recitation of the Prātimokṣa and a common distribution of offerings.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*).
Venerable Sisters of the Sangha, listen!
As has been described regarding the boundaries, the Sangha now establishes at these various locations a single recitation of the precepts and a single distribution of offerings.

"Whichever sisters among you consent to the Sangha binding this boundary so that there shall be a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa and a single distribution of offerings at this place and that place, remain silent; whoever does not consent, speak."
The Sangha has already consented that in this place and that place, there shall be a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa and a single distribution of offerings; the boundary has been established.
Because the Sangha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.

The ritual text for the *karmavācanā* of combining [two areas] into a single *poṣadha* while maintaining separate *lābha* (alms) is as follows: First, each party dissolves their own original boundary; subsequently, the two residences are joined by erecting boundary markers together to form a single boundary.
The entire Saṃgha assembles in one place to perform the *karmavācanā* and establish the boundary.
"Venerable Sisters of the Saṃgha, listen!
[This is] the description of the boundary's directional marks as they have been stated."

If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha listen with patience: the Saṃgha now establishes a common recitation of the Prātimokṣa and separate distribution of offerings at this place and that place.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*).
Venerable Sisters of the Sangha, listen!
As for the boundaries and directional markers as described, the Sangha now, at these locations and those locations, establishes a single *poṣadha* recitation with separate provisions for sustenance.

"Whichever sisters among you approve of the Sangha's formal demarcation within these four boundaries to establish a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa while maintaining separate offerings, remain silent; whoever does not approve, please speak."
The Saṃgha has already consented that within these four boundaries, the same *poṣadha* shall be recited and the distribution of offerings shall be separate.
Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.

If two dwelling places previously shared the recitation of the precepts and the distribution of offerings, or shared the recitation of the precepts while distributing offerings separately, and they later wish to separate again, they should first dissolve the boundary (*sīmā*).
Thereafter, each should individually proclaim the characteristics of their own boundary and, according to the former practice, re-establish the boundaries separately.
The Ritual Text for Establishing Separate Recitation of the Prātimokṣa with a Common Distribution of Offerings: Venerable Sisters, may the Saṃgha listen!

If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent and listen: the Saṃgha now, at this and that residence, shall establish separate recitations of the Prātimokṣa with a common distribution of offerings, for the purpose of protecting the residences.
It is announced as follows:
"Sisters of the Saṃgha, listen!
The Saṃgha now, at this and that residence, establishes a separate recitation of the Prātimokṣa while sharing the same material support, for the sake of protecting the residence."

"Whichever sisters approve of the Saṃgha’s formal resolution to hold separate recitations of the Prātimokṣa at these respective residences, while sharing the same distribution of offerings for the sake of protecting the residences, let them remain silent; whoever does not approve, let her speak."

The Saṃgha has already consented; at this and that residence, the separate recitation of the Prātimokṣa has been performed with a common distribution of offerings for the purpose of protecting the residence.
Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.
